questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: First, I wanted to stay in a country where English is the main language. Second, I wanted to get far away from Denmark. Third, I wanted to go to a place where the culture is "Western" but still different from European culture.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Was a very good experience and would recommend it, but you need to be open-minded and very proactive in order to find new friends.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was somewhat challenging, in the first few weeks after my arrival I sent many e-mails to a lot of people in order to sign up for all the relevant things and fix my accommodation.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not much, I found all the needed information by asking/e-mailing people.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Many options were available. I lived in Ursula Hall, which was a fully catered place, which is what I wanted.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There was no need for cooking where I lived.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: All exchange students should do what they can to live on campus. It really gives you the "real" college experience.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There are a lot of options, both catered and non-catered. I lived in a catered place, but both works just fine.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Was very hard to find the needed information and had to write countless e-mails until I found the correct information.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The process is long and somewhat difficult.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Not much, had to write a lot of e-mails.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I succeded, but only after some struggle.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Ensure you have enough ECTS-points to spend (I could only do 3 courses due to not having enough room on my bachelor's).

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very satisfied, the professors were outstanding and the lecture style worked well.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The academic level was the same as the University of Copenhagen (at least for most of our subjects).

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Same style of teaching, worked well.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Public Sector Economics, International Economics, Corporate Finance.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: International Economics is a complex subject (harder than most UCPH courses). However, this course was also exciting and the lecturer is highly knowledgeable. Corporate Finance is also good for finance-interested people. Public Sector Economics is extremely similar to Mikro1 and Mikro2.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Not any unexpected cost to be honest.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing was a lot more expensive than expected, but this is due to my accommodation being catered.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
Highly satisfied, I played Futsal twice every week for the full semester This was a social event that anyone could join. 
There are many other clubs to join if you want to.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Almost anything you can imagine, there were tons of clubs open to everyone.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I played Futsal, which I loved to do. There is not much going on in the city.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Party is on Thursdays, the city is dead most of the other time.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy even though there were almost no Europeans (or Nordic people) at ANU.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join a club, play sports.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None really.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Very friendly and outgoing people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Join a club/sport
2) Go to lectures/classes even though most of them are recorded
3) Party on Thursdays, so don't have any classes Friday morning.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
If you are confused then level 1000 classes are first year, 2000 are second year, 3000 are third year.
4000 and 8000 level classes are masters/post grad or honours.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Your ability to speak English in a fluent way increases vastly. It is also very rewarding to travel so far and start a new journey of your education.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding the needed information before arriving in Australia.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: You should do it! Just remember to keep an open mind and be very PROACTIVE when it comes to finding new friends.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
